identity.title: IDO1 methylation by EZH2 confers resistance to its targeted therapy in colorectal cancer through tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic rewiring.

content.abstract: Deciphering cancer metabolic reprogramming mechanisms can identify new targets to potentiate EZH2 inhibitor efficacy. Using an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR loss-of-function screen in a CRC mouse model, we pinpointed IDO1 as a key mediator of EZH2 inhibitor resistance. EZH2 blockade remodeled CRC cell metabolism by upregulating IDO1 protein and hyperactivating the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of IDO1 suppressed tumor growth and rescued EZH2 inhibitor resistance in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, EZH2 directly binds and methylates IDO1. Methylation of IDO1 facilitates IDO1 ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Accordingly, EZH2 inhibition stabilizes IDO1, augments tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic flux, and ultimately confers therapeutic resistance. In summary, our study identifies IDO1 as a non-histone substrate of EZH2 methyltransferase activity and validates that disrupting IDO1-mediated tryptophan metabolism is a viable strategy to overcome EZH2 targeted therapy resistance in cancers.
keywords: CRISPR-Cas9 screening in vivo, tryptophan-kynurenine metabolism
